name: 01_publication_overview
title: Policy-BT: from workspace evidence to evolutionary feedback
subtitle: One task, one fixed comparison contract; a growing tournament of generation workspaces.

items.text: Policy-BT: from workspace evidence to evolutionary feedback
One task, one fixed comparison contract; a growing tournament of generation workspaces.
Same task criteria for both workspaces
Earliest decisive stage determines the verdict
Requires relevant images on both sides
Judge A/B and B/A; winners must agree
Absent, unclear or inconsistent → keep tie
A wins  /  B wins  /  tie + evidence
Current reward: rᵢ = σ(θᵢ) if eligible
Earliest losses first; no scores or code
Evolutionary pressure, not a benchmark grade.  σ = logistic function.  Admission verdicts also enter the tournament.

caption: Policy-BT workspace evaluation. (A) The verifier preserves generation artifacts, checks a required reproduction contract and, by default, reruns the submitted shell script in a fresh virtual environment. Goal-grounded reconnaissance establishes fixed, ordered criteria and schema adapters that read actual artifacts. (B) A shared deterministic Python policy compares normalized evidence at the earliest decisive stage. A code tie may be resolved using relevant images from both sides, but only when judgments in both presentation orders agree. Each pair yields a winner or tie, a stage, evidence and side-specific feedback. (C) A regularized Bradley–Terry model fits all pair outcomes and updates each generation’s current reward. Numeric rewards support selection; evidence-grounded diagnoses guide mutation. Ineligible generations receive zero; the verifier does not supply a benchmark grade.

name: 02_methods_detail
title: Policy-BT: comparison contract and tournament mathematics
subtitle: Implementation-level view • task criteria remain fixed while artifact-schema adapters can expand.

items.text: Policy-BT: comparison contract and tournament mathematics
Implementation-level view • task criteria remain fixed while artifact-schema adapters can expand.
Clean venv; move old outputs aside
Fix criteria, stage order and value types
Unknown values do not imply failure
Vision model uses the same goal + criteria
Pair ledger keyed by bundle version
Fit latent θ; publish eligible σ(θ)
Order losses first, then earliest stage
min over θ:  −Σ [yᵢⱼ log pᵢⱼ + (1−yᵢⱼ) log(1−pᵢⱼ)] + ½ Σ θᵢ²
Unit Gaussian prior • rᵢ = σ(θᵢ) versus a neutral-strength opponent; ineligible rᵢ = 0.
No-pair eligible baseline: 0.5.  Instrument error: unscored, not reward 0.  Reruns are trusted local shell execution, not an OS sandbox.

caption: Implementation and scoring details. Snapshot admission precedes artifact comparison. Task criteria, order and representation remain fixed; schema adapters can expand and instrument code can be repaired without changing the success definition. The restricted interpreter checks reverse-order consistency, self-ties and repeated execution. Vision is conditional on a deterministic tie and relevant images from both sides. The tournament contains every unordered generation pair, including execution-admission outcomes. For each ordered representation (i,j) of an unordered pair, y is 1, 1/2 or 0 for an i win, tie or loss. A unit-precision zero-mean Gaussian prior regularizes the Bradley–Terry strengths. The published reward is the logistic probability of beating a neutral-strength opponent, except ineligible generations are forced to zero. Instrument failures are unscored. Pair results are keyed by bundle version. A bundle-version change recomputes every pair; in the current implementation, a new eligible generation changes that version through its schema assignment and visual selection. Current ratings refresh while historical arrival scores and previously emitted gradients are preserved. The first sum runs once over each unordered pair; minimization is over the full strength vector θ. An eligible generation beats an ineligible one; two ineligible generations tie.

name: 03_presentation
title: One policy. Two evidence channels. A tournament reward.
subtitle: Policy-BT evaluates scientific outputs across workflow generations—not against hidden benchmark answers.

items.text: One policy. Two evidence channels. A tournament reward.
Policy-BT evaluates scientific outputs across workflow generations—not against hidden benchmark answers.
Goal-defined criteria, fixed across the task
Earliest decisive stage → win / loss / tie
Reward ≠ raw win rate ≠ benchmark grade
Code decides first. Images can break a tie. Bradley–Terry converts the verdict history into a current reward.

caption: Presentation overview. Preserved workspace evidence is admitted and normalized, compared by one task-specific deterministic policy, and optionally judged visually after code ties. The full pair-verdict history feeds a regularized Bradley–Terry fit. All current generation rewards refresh; evidence-grounded feedback guides subsequent mutation. Neither raw win rate nor hidden benchmark labels define the reward. Admission verdicts precede the two artifact-evidence channels and also enter the tournament.
